text:
claire: FYI kicking off onboarding for cust Nereid's LoRA (nereid-adapter-v1) layered onto redwood/atlas-13b-std. adapter applies head-gating + small layer-norm rescale. running quick 400-sample evalpack now.
diego: acceptance gates?
claire: parity on extraction EM, no currency/token non-breaking-space (NBSP) insertions, date normalization parity. allow <=2.5% EM drop.
sophia: quick micro-quant: fp16 merge looks ok, int8 small delta, int4 merged artifact shows non-breaking-space inserted before punctuation in some locales (e.g. "123,45" -> "123 ,45") and occasional emoji tokenization jitter affecting chat-like examples. stats: baseline EM=92.3%, nereid-int4 EM=88.9% (delta -3.4%), ll_mean delta -0.26.
bench-bot: infra tokenizer=tok-1.4.0, cust tokenizer artifact pinned tok-1.3.0.
diego: try re-running with cust tok pinned and stitch overlay instead of hard merge. also run quant-calib using cust token distribution.
sophia: re-ran with tok-1.3.0 and stitch overlay: EM improved to 90.6%, NBSP anomalies down from 11/400 to 4/400, emoji jitter reduced but not gone. looks like norm-rescale pushes some punctuation embeddings across int4 bin edges.
claire: plan: 1) prefer stitch overlay for canary, 2) export fp16 and run quant-aware calibration with customer's tokenizer+locale corpus (5k samples), 3) collect per-token entropy delta and bin-occupancy histograms, 4) prepare atlas-13b-int4-safe fallback and runtime routing if EM_drop>2%.
diego: queued canary id=nereid-canary-4456 on dedicated atlas pool, stitch=true, tok_pin=tok-1.3.0, calib_samples=5000, ETA ~3h.
eval-bot: micro-eval summary: quality_regression=true, primary_metric=EM_drop, value=3.4%, ll_delta=-0.26, token_nbsp_anomalies=11/400 -> recommended_actions=["stitch+tok_pin+quant_calib","collect-bin_histograms","run_2k_eval_before_canary"]. :robot_face:
claire: leaving canary running. when finished, post CSV + 10 counterexamples and we'll decide staged rollout vs safe-fallback.
